newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up but skeptics remain.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up but skeptics remain.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures, buoyed by firmer cash and forecasts for colder weather next week, ended higher across the board Friday in moderate activity, but some expected the rally to be short-lived.
April climbed 6.1 cents to close at $1.947 per million British thermal units. May settled seven cents higher at $2.023. Other deferreds ended up by 0.2 to 6.2 cents.

"There was a lot of short covering due to unexpected cash market strength ahead of the weekend, but it should be short lived. There's no long-term weather support," said one Midwest trader, adding an April break to $2.04-06 was a great sale.

While downside momentum seemed exhausted, raising the possibility of more technical rebound, traders said any move up should be difficult to sustain, with milder spring temperatures ahead and inventories at comfortable levels.
But near-term, traders said physical and paper prices should garner some support from the return next week of more winter-like weather to the Midwest and Northeast.
Technical traders said the market remained range-bound, with April resistance still at $2 and $2.04, while support was seen in the $1.78-1.80 area and at the $1.701 contract low.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained more than five cents Friday to the mid-to-high $1.80s. Midcon pipes were talked up slightly to the mid-to-high $1.70s. New York city gate swing gas slipped into the teens.
The 12-month strip gained 5.1 cents to $2.117. NYMEX said an estimated 44,836 contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 30,963.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Friday.

On the KCBT, April finished seven cents higher at $1.72, while deferreds ended up by three to six cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.9 cent to 22.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 248 lots changed hands, down sharply from Thursday's total of 834.
